column2: Fumigation with neem; one should anoint with bhutogra, raji and sarjarasa; the offering should be removed outside: parched rice, kulmasha and kavaka-rice.
So the fumigation and other rites should continue up to thirteen days. The seizer Putana-Sankuli seizes the one-month-old child:
crying like a crow, breathing, smell of urine, closing of the eyes. Bathing him with cow-urine and fumigating with a cow's tooth;
one should give yellow cloth, red garland and scent, an oil lamp; threefold pudding, liquor, and fourfold sesame and masha;
under a karanja tree in Yama's direction for seven days one should remove the offering with them. The two-month-old: Mukuta, with a cold, chill body,
vomiting, dry mouth and the like; flowers, scents and cloth; cake, rice, lamp, black water and the like, fumigation.
In the third, Gomukhi: sleep, crying with feces and urine; barley, priyangu, palana, kulmasha, vegetable and rice;
milk should be given earlier; at midday fumigation with ghee; a bath with the five-bhanga; in the fourth, Pingala removes distress:
body thin and cold, foul smell, dryness — he surely dies. The fifth, Lalana: limb-weakness and dryness of the mouth,
yellow Apana; offering with fish and the like on the right. In the sixth month, Pankaja: movements, crying, distorted voice;
an offering of fish, meat, liquor, cooked food, flowers, scents and the like. In the seventh, without food, foul smell and toothache and the like;
offering with ground meat, liquor and meat in the eighth, Yamuna: eruptions and wasting and the like — one should not have its treatment done.
In the ninth, afflicted by Kumbhakarni, feverish, vomiting; crying; an offering of meat, kulmasha, liquor and the like in the Vaishvaka.
In the tenth, Tapasi: movements, fasting, closing the eyes; bell and banner; ground (offering) is told; offering of liquor and meat equal.
The eleventh, Rakshasi: affliction of the eyes and the like; no treatment. In the twelfth, Chanchala: breathing, movements of terror and the like;
the offering earlier, at midday, with kulmasha and the like, sesame and the like. In the second year, Yatana: torment, crying and the like;
offering with sesame, meat and liquor and meat; bath and the rest as before. In the third, Rodani: trembling, crying, bloody urine;
jaggery rice, sesame cake, an image made of sesame paste; sesame bath with five leaves, fumigation with rajaphala bark.
In the fourth, Chataka: swelling, fever, weakness of all limbs; offering with fish, meat, sesame and the like, and bath and fumigation.
In the fifth year Chanchala: fever, terror, weakness of limbs; offering with meat, rice and the like; fumigation with ram's horn;
water with leaves of palasha, udumbara, ashvattha, vata and bilva. In the sixth year: running, dryness, distaste, weakness of limbs;
offering with the earlier seven days'; fumigation and bath with bhangaka. In the seventh, Yamuna: vomiting, reluctant speech, laughing, crying;
offering with meat, padya, liquor and the like; bath and fumigation. In the eighth, Jatavedas: fasting and crying;
offering with kushara, cake, curds and the like; bath and fumigation. In the ninth year, Kala: slapping of arms, roaring, fear;
offering would be with kushara, cakes, barley meal, kulmasha and pudding. In the tenth year, Kalahamsi: burning, thinness of limbs, fever;
one should remove the offering for five nights with pulika cakes and curd rice. Neem fumigation and kushtha paste; the eleventh seizer
Devaduti: harsh speech; offering, anointing and the like as before. Balika in the twelfth: offering, anointing and the like as before.
In the thirteenth, Vayavi: weakness of mouth and outer limbs; offering with red rice, scents, garlands and the like; one should bathe with five leaves;
fumigation with raji and neem leaves; Yakshini in the fourteenth: movements, colic, fever, burning; offering with meat-eating and the like;
bath and the rest as before for pacification; Mundika affliction in the fifteenth: its signs: constant flow of blood; one should make the Mothers' treatment.
Vanari in the sixteenth: falling to the ground, sleep, constant fever; with pudding and the like three nights, offering, bath and the rest as before.
Gandhavati in the seventeenth: agitation of the limbs, crying; offering with kulmasha and the like; bath, fumigation, anointing and the rest as before.

Putanas are lords of days; Sukumarikas lords of years. "Om homage to all Mothers: consume the conjunction of child-affliction, eat eat, chut chut, burst burst, throb throb, seize seize, draw draw" — thus the accomplished form commands. "Hari, Hari, make faultless the girl, boy, woman or man, through the approach to all seizers. Chamunda, homage to the goddess, hrum hrum hrim, go away, go away, wicked seizers hrum, so — let the house-seizers go elsewhere on the path; Rudra commands." In all child-seizures this mantra is accomplishing all wishes.

Om homage to the Lady Chamunda: release release the offering, the girl; take the offering, take, victory victory, dwell dwell. In all giving of offerings this mantra is recited as protection. May they protect and release the child from fever: Brahma, Vishnu, Shiva, Skanda, Gaura, Gauri, Lakshmi, the hosts and the rest.
At river confluences, empty houses, burrow doors, single trees, the seizers seize men, prosperity, a sleeping woman and a pregnant one;
one near flowers who is naked and bathes after her period. Insult among men, enmity, obstruction, reversal of fortune,
transgression of the gods, teacher, dharma and the rest of good conduct; falling from a mountain or tree and the like, shaking the hair repeatedly;
one who weeps, dances, has red eyes, makes the "hum" sound — a man seized by a favoring spirit; agitated, afflicted by colic and burning, tormented by hunger and thirst, with headache;
one who begs "give, give" is a man seized by a Balika; a man who desires women, garlands, enjoyment and bathing is seized by an amorous one.
Mahasudarshana, pervading the sky, with a branch-nose; Patala-Narasimha and the rest, Chandi mantras are seizure-crushers.
Prishni, hing, vacha, chakra, shirisha — the supreme dear; the god bearing noose and goad, with rosary and skull;
bearing a khatvanga, lotus and power, four-faced, within and without, on the khatvanga-lotus in the solar disc,
having worshipped with the Adityas and the rest, at sunrise one should give the arghya. "Shvasa, visha, agni, vipra, kundi, hrillekha" — Bhrigu complete,
to Arka, bhur bhuvah svah, Jvalini, Kulamudgara; lotus-seated, red, in red cloth, radiant, universal;
generous, bearing a lotus in both arms, gentle, adorned in all limbs; the red heart-mantras and the rest gentle, boon-giving, lotus-bearing;
cloth like a mass of lightning; Moon white, gentle; Mars red; Mercury likewise; Jupiter yellow; Venus white; Saturn
black like charcoal; Rahu smoky; Ketu is declared. The left thigh and left hand, ends; the right hand granting fearlessness;
their seeds begin with their own names. Having purified both hands with the weapon, one should place on thumbs and the rest, palm and eyes the heart-mantra and the rest pervasively;
with the three root seeds one should place the life-meditation with limbs. Having washed the vessel with the weapon, having filled it with water with the root mantra,
having placed scent, flowers and rice, one should consecrate durva and arghya. Having sprinkled oneself with it, and the worship substance surely,
abundant, spotless, essential, to be worshipped, supreme bliss. One should arrange the seat and the rest with the heart in the middle and the corners;
on the seat with the heart in the middle, in directions and corners; on the seat the heart-lotus, and in the filaments eight powers:
vam Dipta, "vim" Sukshma, "vum" Jaya, "vum" Bhadrika, "vem" Vibhuti, "vaim" Vimala, "vom" Amogha-vidyuta,
vaum Sarvatomukhi, "vam" the seat — having worshipped, one should worship the Sun. Having invoked, one should give water for the feet and the rest with the heart and six limbs, of good vow.
The two kha-letters, Dandin and Chanda, with marrow joined with teeth, flesh long, aged wind, heart — this gives all of the Sun.
Fire, Ishvara, Rakshasa, wind in the directions are to be worshipped, with the heart and the rest; with their own mantras standing within the pericarp; in the directions the weapon in front equally.
In the east and the other directions Moon, Mercury, Jupiter and Venus are to be worshipped. One should perform nasal treatment, collyrium and the like with goat's urine and seizure-removers.
With patha, pathya, vacha, shigru, rock salt and the three pungents separately, with fruit, ghee cooked in an adhaka of goat's milk removes all seizures.
Vrishchikali, phali, kushtha, salts and sarngaka — one should feed that water for destroying epilepsy.
One should give milk made from decoction of vidari, kusha, kasha and sugarcane; in a drona with yashti and kushmanda juice, with ghee prepared;

pancha-gavya ghee likewise — hear the combination that removes fever. "Om, we know the ash-weapon; we meditate on the one-tusked; may that fever impel us." One should lick krishna, ushana, nisha, rasna, grapes, oil and jaggery;
or for one with asthma bharngi with yashti, honey and ghee; patha, tikta, kana, bharngi, or lick with honey;
dhatri, vishva, krishna, mustaka, date, magadhi, pivara — these three destroy hiccup; one should lick with honey.

In jaundice one should drink the juice of jira, mandukaparni, turmeric and amalaka. The three pungents, padmaka, triphala, vidanga, devadaru, rasna powder in equal parts with sugar lumps, having eaten it surely removes cough.
In the northeast, the nirmalya for Yama; the radiance blazed for Chanda; gorochana, saffron, water, red scent, rice and sprouts,
bamboo seeds, barley, rice, shyamaka, sesame, mustard; having given with hibiscus flowers, one should hold it on the head in vessels;
having gone to the ground on both knees, one should offer arghya to the Sun. Having worshipped the planets with nine pots consecrated by one's own mantra,
a bath for pacification of planets and the rest; having recited to the Sun one obtains all. Victory in battle, with fire, fault of seed, with the bindu,
having placed from head to feet, having worshipped the root with the mudra, and one's own limbs as placed, one should contemplate oneself as the Sun.
Meditation in killing and stopping is yellow; in nourishing white; in killing the enemy black; one should bewilder like Indra's bow.
One who is always devoted to consecration, recitation, meditation, worship and oblation becomes splendid, victorious in heart, glorious; at the ocean and the like he gains victory.
Having placed this on betel and the like and having recited, one should give ushira. Touching by the hand placed with the seed is remembered as for bringing under control.
A woman desiring a son should drink with milk the root of durva or ashvagandha; kaunti, Lakshmi's shipha, dhatri, vajra, lodhra, banyan sprout,
ghee and milk should be drunk in the fertile season for a son; she (gains) heaven. A woman desiring a son should drink milk, shrimula with banyan sprout;
juice of shri, banyan sprout, devi herbs as a nasal drop she should take; shripadma root, milk, with ashvattha and uttara roots.
